title: Remonstrant rousing grace: illumination of the mind acting on the will
source_text: XXXVI. Nam ibi per gratiam excitantem intelligere se dicunt gratiosam & impromeritam Dei ac Spiritus Sancti operationem, quae primum intellectum rerum salutarium cognitione imbuit, & illustrat, adeoque veritati divinae assentiri facit, & secundo in ipsam voluntatem agit per eandem illuminationem & sensus verbo comprehensos.
pass_a_gloss: XXXVI. For there they say they understand by rousing grace the gracious and unmerited operation of God and the Holy Spirit, which first imbues the intellect with the knowledge of saving things, and illumines it, and so makes it assent to divine truth, and secondly acts on the will itself through the same illumination and the senses comprised in the word.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXXVI. There they say that by rousing grace they mean the gracious and unmerited working of God and the Holy Spirit.

First it fills the intellect with knowledge of the things of salvation and enlightens it, and so brings it to assent to divine truth. Second, it acts on the will itself through that same enlightenment and through the meanings contained in the word.
